project.name: Cloudflare Worker Geocoding API (GeoNames)
project.summary: A Cloudflare Workers (TypeScript) API that accepts LLM-generated location strings, normalizes and resolves them via GeoNames, returns deterministic coordinates + canonical metadata, and caches results in D1 with a KV hot-cache for use in a Next.js mapping app.

items.description: Assume GeoNames usage (username-based) is available for server-side geocoding and within expected rate/quota limits for the MVP.
steps: Confirm a valid GeoNames username exists and can successfully call the GeoNames API from a non-browser environment.
Document the expected daily/hourly request volume and confirm it is compatible with GeoNames limits for the MVP usage.
If the quota/limits are insufficient, record the required mitigation (additional provider, stronger caching, batch, or throttling).
items.notes: If limits are too low, add a second provider or strengthen cache strategy before production rollout.

items.description: Validate the expected input patterns and edge cases from the LLM (Saudi-centric + global) to tune parsing and scoring rules.
steps: Collect at least 30 real examples of location strings produced by the LLM (including city+region+country, region+country, country-only, and multi-area).
Identify at least 10 problematic examples (misspellings, swapped token order, extra punctuation, alternative country names like KSA).
Produce a short list of acceptance examples to use as fixtures for unit/E2E tests.

items.description: Define the v1 API contract (request/response types) and versioning rules for deterministic consumption by Next.js.
steps: Confirm `POST /v1/geocode` accepts `{ "text": string }` and rejects missing/empty text with HTTP 400.
Confirm response matches the agreed shape: input/raw + normalizedKey, canonical fields, optional point/bbox, confidence 0..1, flags, provider, cache.hit.
Document v1 stability rules: additive changes allowed; breaking changes require `/v2`.

items.description: Define a consistent error response format and status code mapping for client-safe handling.
steps: Specify an error JSON shape (e.g., `{error:{code,message,details?}}`) and use it for all non-2xx responses except OPTIONS.
Map at least: 400 invalid input, 401 missing/invalid API key, 403 origin not allowed, 405 wrong method, 429 rate limited, 502 provider failure, 500 internal error.
Verify the client can distinguish retryable errors (429/502) from non-retryable errors (400/401/403/405).

items.description: Specify deterministic normalization and cache key rules to ensure repeatable geocoding results over time.
steps: Given identical raw text inputs, confirm the produced normalizedKey is identical across repeated calls and deployments.
Given inputs differing only in casing/whitespace/diacritics/punctuation, confirm the normalizedKey is identical.
Document tie-break rules for candidates so the same best candidate is chosen deterministically when scores match closely.

items.description: Create D1 schema migrations for geocode cache and minimal event logging tables.
steps: Apply migration to create `geocode_cache` with a unique constraint on `input_norm_key` and an index on `country_iso2`.
Apply migration to create `geocode_events` with fields needed for minimal audit (raw input, norm key, status, provider, truncated provider_response, created_at).
Verify migrations are idempotent (re-running them does not fail).

items.description: Set up Wrangler configuration for Worker, D1 binding, KV binding, environment variables, and secrets.
steps: Verify Wrangler config includes D1 binding `DB` and KV binding `GEO_KV` and they are accessible from the Worker runtime.
Store `GEONAMES_USERNAME` and `API_KEY` as secrets and confirm they are not logged or returned in errors.
Set `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` as a comma-separated allowlist and confirm the Worker reads it correctly.

items.description: Initialize Worker TypeScript project using Hono and implement route skeleton for /health and /v1/geocode.
steps: Deploy a minimal Worker that responds 200 on `GET /health` with a small JSON payload.
Verify `POST /v1/geocode` returns 501 (or a placeholder error) before feature implementation, using the standard error format.
Verify unsupported routes return 404 in the standard error format.

items.description: Implement strict CORS allowlist for allowed origins and correct preflight handling for all routes.
steps: From an allowed Origin, verify browser preflight (OPTIONS) returns appropriate CORS headers for `POST /v1/geocode`.
From a disallowed Origin, verify the response does not include permissive CORS headers and results in a blocked browser call.
Verify allowed headers include at least `content-type` and `x-api-key`.

items.description: Require `x-api-key` authentication for all non-health endpoints and ensure safe comparison and error handling.
steps: Call `GET /health` without `x-api-key` and verify it returns 200.
Call `POST /v1/geocode` without `x-api-key` and verify it returns 401 with standard error JSON and no sensitive details.
Call `POST /v1/geocode` with an incorrect `x-api-key` and verify 401; with correct key verify authentication passes.

items.description: Harden request handling: method restrictions, JSON parsing, payload limits, and input validation.
steps: Send invalid JSON to `POST /v1/geocode` and verify HTTP 400 with standard error JSON.
Send `{ "text": "" }` and verify HTTP 400; send overly long text (e.g., > 512 chars) and verify HTTP 400.
Send `GET /v1/geocode` and verify HTTP 405 with standard error JSON.

items.description: Apply Cloudflare rate limiting rules per API key to protect GeoNames quotas and mitigate abuse.
steps: Define a rate limit policy (requests/minute per API key) and document it as an operational control.
Trigger the rate limit in a test scenario and verify the API returns 429 with standard error JSON.
Verify rate limiting does not affect `GET /health`.
items.notes: Implement via Cloudflare WAF/Rate Limiting configuration; exact mechanism may depend on account features.

items.description: Implement deterministic parsing of comma-separated tokens and multi-area detection.
steps: Input 'Riyadh, Riyadh Region, Saudi Arabia' yields parsed city='Riyadh', admin1='Riyadh Region', countryText='Saudi Arabia', isMultiArea=false.
Input 'Najran Region, Saudi Arabia' yields parsed admin1='Najran Region', countryText='Saudi Arabia', city unset, isMultiArea=false.
Input containing 'Multiple Areas' (case-insensitive) yields isMultiArea=true and granularityHint='multi'.

items.description: Implement token normalization utilities (casefold, diacritics removal, punctuation trimming, whitespace/hyphen normalization).
steps: Given tokens with extra spaces/punctuation, confirm normalized tokens are stable and consistent (e.g., 'Riyāḍh.' -> 'riyadh').
Verify normalization does not delete meaningful alphabetic characters (e.g., keeps letters and numbers).
Confirm normalization output is used for key generation and similarity scoring, while raw input is preserved.

items.description: Resolve country to ISO2 using offline mappings (accept ISO2/ISO3 and common English names) before provider calls.
steps: Input with ISO2 country (e.g., 'Riyadh, SA') resolves to countryIso2='SA'.
Input with ISO3 country (e.g., 'Riyadh, SAU') resolves to countryIso2='SA'.
Input with country name (e.g., 'Saudi Arabia') resolves to countryIso2='SA' without an external call when supported by offline mapping.

items.description: Fallback to GeoNames country search (PCLI) to resolve countryIso2 when offline mapping fails.
steps: Provide a countryText not recognized offline and verify the system calls GeoNames with country-level constraints and extracts a valid ISO2 code when possible.
If no country match exists, verify geocoding returns HTTP 200 with low confidence and `flags.ambiguous=true` (or a clear failure code if preferred in design), per documented behavior.
Verify provider timeouts produce a retryable error (502) rather than hanging.

items.description: Generate normalized cache keys in the format `<countryIso2>|<admin1_norm>|<city_norm>|<multi_flag>`.
steps: Input 'Riyadh, Saudi Arabia' produces normalizedKey 'SA||riyadh|'.
Input 'Eastern Province, Saudi Arabia' produces normalizedKey 'SA|eastern province||'.
Input 'Multiple Areas, Saudi Arabia' produces normalizedKey 'SA|||multi'.

items.description: Implement KV hot-cache read/write of the full response with a 30-day TTL and deterministic serialization.
steps: On cache hit, verify response returns with `cache.hit=true` and matches the stored payload exactly.
On cache miss, verify the response is written to KV and can be retrieved on a subsequent call within TTL.
Verify KV entries expire after TTL (or via configuration inspection if TTL expiry cannot be forced quickly).

items.description: Implement D1 lookup by `input_norm_key` and map stored rows back into the API response shape.
steps: Insert a known cache record and verify `POST /v1/geocode` returns it correctly with `cache.hit=true` (D1 hit when KV is empty).
Verify bbox and flags are correctly parsed from stored JSON strings (if stored as text).
Verify missing optional fields in storage do not break response (null-safe mapping).

items.description: Create provider abstraction (interfaces + pipeline) supporting GeoNames first and easy addition of future providers.
steps: Verify the provider interface can return a list of candidates with normalized fields (lat/lon/country/admin1/city, featureClass/featureCode).
Verify the pipeline can call providers in order and aggregate candidates into a single list.
Verify a provider timeout leads to a pipeline-controlled failure behavior rather than an unhandled exception.

items.description: Implement GeoNames provider city-level query using searchJSON with populated place filters and fuzzy matching.
steps: Given a city+country input, verify a GeoNames request is made that favors populated places and includes fuzzy matching.
Verify the provider returns candidates with lat/lon and includes providerId (GeoNameId) when present.
Verify provider fetch uses a strict timeout and returns a controlled error on timeout.

items.description: Implement GeoNames provider region-level query using ADM1 filters and fuzzy matching.
steps: Given admin1+country input, verify a GeoNames request is made that targets ADM1 regions (feature class A, ADM1).
Verify returned candidates include admin1 and countryIso2 where available.
Verify empty results are handled gracefully (no exception) and are eligible for fallback behavior.

items.description: Implement GeoNames provider country-level query using PCLI filter and return centroid and bbox when available.
steps: Given country-only input, verify a GeoNames request targets country-level results (PCLI) and returns a candidate with a representative point.
Verify bbox is extracted when present and mapped into `[west,south,east,north]`.
Verify provider returns an empty list (not error) when no match exists.

items.description: Implement candidate scoring (country/admin/city similarity, feature type match, importance proxy) and compute confidence 0..1.
steps: Given an input with countryIso2, verify candidates with matching country receive higher scores than mismatched countries.
Given an input with admin1/city tokens, verify similarity scoring increases score for closer matches and decreases for mismatches.
Verify confidence is clamped to [0,1] and decreases appropriately when only weak matches exist.

items.description: Select best candidate deterministically, apply ambiguity rule (top2 within 0.05), and set flags accordingly.
steps: When two candidates score within 0.05, verify the response sets `flags.ambiguous=true` and reduces confidence per documented behavior.
Verify tie-break behavior is deterministic (e.g., score desc, importance/population desc, providerId asc) and stable across runs.
Verify candidates with known country mismatch are rejected when countryIso2 is known.

items.description: Compute granularity and canonical fields (city/region/country/multi) and generate displayName consistently.
steps: City input yields `granularity='city'` and canonical includes city and countryIso2; region input yields `granularity='region'` and canonical includes admin1 and countryIso2.
Country-only input yields `granularity='country'` and canonical includes countryIso2; multi-area yields `granularity='multi'` and sets `flags.multiArea=true`.
Verify displayName is stable and consistent (e.g., 'City, Region, Country' or best available combination).

items.description: Implement provider fallback detection and validation flags (adminMismatch, providerFallback) without breaking determinism.
steps: When strict query returns none and relaxed query returns results, verify `flags.providerFallback=true`.
If input admin1 exists and best candidate admin1 similarity is below threshold, verify `flags.adminMismatch=true`.
Verify flags are persisted in cache responses (subsequent calls return the same flags).

items.description: Implement multi-area behavior using a country centroid point while marking `multiArea=true` and avoiding city-level claims.
steps: Input 'Multiple Areas, Saudi Arabia' returns `granularity='multi'`, includes `flags.multiArea=true`, and provides a point representing the country centroid (or best available country-level point).
Verify canonical.city and canonical.admin1 are unset for multi-area responses unless explicitly provided and validated (should be unset for MVP).
Verify UI-facing fields do not imply a specific city location when multiArea is true.

items.description: Implement D1 upsert for geocode_cache with updated timestamps and stable storage of bbox/flags JSON.
steps: On first miss, verify a new row is inserted with input_raw, input_norm_key, canonical fields, point/bbox, provider, confidence, flags, created_at, updated_at.
On subsequent calls (same key) after a recompute, verify the existing row is updated (updated_at changes; created_at remains).
Verify the unique constraint on input_norm_key prevents duplicates and the system still returns a single deterministic result.

items.description: Log minimal geocoding events to D1 (hit/miss/error/ambiguous) with truncated provider payload for debugging.
steps: On a cache hit, verify an optional event is recorded only if configured (or record misses/errors only, per MVP decision); confirm behavior matches documentation.
On a miss that results in a successful provider lookup, verify a `miss` (or `resolved`) status is recorded with provider name.
On provider errors/timeouts, verify an `error` status is recorded and provider_response is truncated to a safe length.

items.description: Add structured logging for request IDs, cache status, provider timings, and error categories without leaking secrets.
steps: Verify logs include a request correlation ID and record whether the response was KV hit, D1 hit, or provider call.
Verify logs include provider latency measurements for uncached calls.
Verify logs never contain API keys, GeoNames username, or full raw provider responses beyond the truncation policy.

items.description: Implement end-to-end /v1/geocode flow: normalize → resolve country → cache lookup (KV/D1) → GeoNames → score/select → persist → return.
steps: Call `POST /v1/geocode` with 'Riyadh, Saudi Arabia' and verify 200 response includes point, canonical fields, provider name, and confidence in [0,1].
Repeat the same request and verify `cache.hit=true` and the response is identical (except any explicitly documented cache metadata).
Call with an input that cannot be resolved and verify behavior matches the documented error/low-confidence policy (no crashes, consistent error format if failing).

items.description: Finalize /health endpoint for operational monitoring and smoke checks.
steps: Verify `GET /health` returns 200 with a small JSON including at least `{status:'ok'}` (and optionally version/uptime).
Verify /health does not require an API key and does not return CORS headers beyond what is required (safe defaults).
Verify /health remains responsive even when provider calls are failing (no provider dependency).

items.description: Define and validate basic performance targets for cached and uncached requests in Workers.
steps: With KV hit, verify typical response time is low enough for interactive use (target p95 documented for your environment).
With D1 hit (KV empty), verify response time remains acceptable and stable under moderate load.
With provider call, verify provider timeout is enforced and the API returns a response/error within the bounded time.
items.notes: Exact p95 thresholds depend on environment; document and validate.

items.description: Add unit tests for parsing, normalization, multi-area detection, and normalized key generation using collected fixtures.
steps: Run tests confirming all fixture inputs produce the expected parsed fields and normalizedKey.
Include negative tests for empty tokens, extra commas, and unusual punctuation.
Verify tests pass in CI and locally with deterministic outcomes.

items.description: Add unit tests for country resolution (offline ISO2/ISO3/name) and GeoNames PCLI fallback behavior via mocked fetch.
steps: Verify ISO2 and ISO3 inputs resolve correctly without network calls.
Verify unknown country name triggers a mocked GeoNames call and resolves ISO2 when mock response is valid.
Verify provider timeout mock results in a controlled error outcome.

items.description: Add unit tests for scoring, deterministic selection, ambiguity threshold handling, and flag assignment.
steps: Provide mocked candidate sets where top2 are within 0.05 and verify `ambiguous=true` and confidence reduction policy is applied.
Provide mocked candidates with country mismatch and verify they are rejected when input countryIso2 is known.
Verify tie-break produces identical selected candidate across repeated test runs.

items.description: Add integration tests for /v1/geocode using mocked GeoNames responses, validating cache flow (KV then D1).
steps: First call returns provider-derived result and sets `cache.hit=false`.
Second call returns `cache.hit=true` from KV (simulate KV hit) and matches the first response payload.
If KV is cleared, verify D1 hit returns the same cached payload with `cache.hit=true`.

items.description: Run smoke tests against live GeoNames for a small curated set of real inputs and record outputs for regression.
steps: Deploy with real secrets and call /v1/geocode for at least 15 curated inputs; verify 200 responses and reasonable confidence values.
Include at least 3 ambiguous cases and verify ambiguous flag behavior matches the selected policy.
Store outputs as golden results for regression comparison (acknowledging provider data can change over time).

items.description: Validate security controls: API key auth, CORS allowlist, and rate limiting behavior.
steps: Verify unauthorized requests to /v1/geocode return 401 without CORS leakage for disallowed origins.
Verify allowed origin + valid API key succeeds; disallowed origin fails in browser context (CORS blocked).
Trigger rate limit and verify 429 with standard error JSON and no provider calls being made when already limited.

items.description: Document API usage for Next.js integration (request examples, response fields, and rendering rules by granularity).
steps: Provide a minimal example of calling `POST /v1/geocode` from Next.js (server action or route handler) including required headers.
Document how to render markers for `city/region/country/multi` including multi-area disclaimer behavior.
Document caching expectations and that results become deterministic after first resolution due to D1+KV caching.

items.description: Write operational runbook: secrets, environment variables, migrations, rate limiting setup, troubleshooting, and log/event interpretation.
steps: Document all required secrets/vars and where they are configured (Wrangler + Cloudflare dashboard).
Document migration application steps for D1 and how to verify table/index existence.
Document common failure modes (GeoNames timeouts, ambiguous results, country mismatch) and where to see evidence (logs/events).

items.description: Deploy the Worker with proper bindings/secrets and verify rollback procedure.
steps: Deploy the Worker and verify /health and /v1/geocode work end-to-end with valid secrets and bindings.
Verify allowed origins are properly configured for the deployment.
Document and validate rollback by deploying a known previous version and confirming service restoration.

items.description: Add CI checks (lint, typecheck, tests) and a deploy workflow.
steps: Verify CI runs lint + typecheck + unit/integration tests on pull requests.
Verify deploy runs only after checks pass.
Verify deploy uses the correct secrets and bindings.
